title: Vectorize-v2 gated activation: batching, rerank alignment, and staged retirement plan
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Introduce a gated, tenant-aware activation for Vectorize-v2 (new embedding + reranker variant) that prioritizes quality alignment with existing rerank pipelines while preserving latency SLOs and scaling predictably. This ticket covers integration testing, batching configuration, KV-prefetch telemetry, canary rollout plumbing, per-tenant throttles, and a clear retirement path for the legacy vectorizer. Goals: verify semantic parity for top-k reranker signals, keep p50 generation latency within 1.5x of baseline under 99th percentile traffic, and provide automated fallback to stable model variants.
acceptance_criteria: Automated semantic regression tests pass across 10 representative tenant prompt sets with delta < 2% on rerank NDCG@10
End-to-end p50/p95 latency for embedding-only path stays within configured SLO (p50 < 35ms, p95 < 120ms) during 2x baseline QPS load tests
Batching config (max_batch_size, batch_timeout_ms) auto-tunes for each pool and documented in the tuning runbook
Canary rollout plumbing supports per-tenant weight, shadow traffic, and automatic rollback on quality or latency regressions
Fallback policy routes to prior vectorizer variant without request loss and preserves tenant affinity
tasks: Wire Vectorize-v2 model into embed and rerank gateway adapters
Implement tenant affinity and per-tenant batch caps in gateway
Add KV-prefetch hook for rerank to reduce cold KV hits
Create semantic regression harness and canonical prompt sets
Run staged canary: 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with monitoring gates
Add observability: per-model NDCG, avg token cost, per-tenant p95 latency
Document rollback and deprecation policy for legacy vectorizer
notes: This approach aims to avoid a hard swap; we prefer progressive tenant opt-ins tied to quality fences. We will leverage existing adaptive batching hooks from the serving runtime and extend telemetry to capture rerank delta metrics. Initial capacity estimate uses a hot/warm split to keep memory pressure low on multi-tenant hosts.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: New embedding shifts rerank ordering for edge queries — Mitigation: run diffing on holdout dataset and gate canary until NDCG threshold met
Risk: Larger batches increase tail latency for small requests — Mitigation: per-tenant max_batch_size and low-latency bypass for <10ms queries
Risk: KV cache churn during model swap — Mitigation: pre-warm KV entries and use rolling host-level cache warming
telemetry_requirements: Batch size distribution and batch_timeout percentiles
KV cache hit/miss ratio and prefetch latency
